problem: one fix split into two clauses; second clause redundant
old_why: Why: conjunction (comma splice -> "so"); punctuation (comma -> "so" after it).
new_why: Why: conjunction (comma splice -> ", so").

problem: trigger quote omits "nearest" (does not match user words)
old_why: Why: word order ("where is the tea stall" -> "where the tea stall is").
new_why: Why: word order ("where is the nearest tea stall" -> "where the nearest tea stall is").

problem: one fix split into two clauses (duplicate subject-verb clause)
old_why: Why: continuous tense ("birds flies" -> "are flying"); subject-verb agreement ("flies" -> "are").
new_why: Why: continuous tense ("birds flies" -> "birds are flying").

problem: corrected text changed vs source ("new in" -> "new to") though source was not wrong; reverted, clause dropped
old_why: Why: pronoun ("Myself Ritika" -> "I am Ritika"); preposition ("new in" -> "new to").
new_why: Why: pronoun ("Myself Ritika" -> "I am Ritika").

problem: article clause covered the plural/hyphen fix too; clauses overlapped
old_why: Why: article ("is ten years old boy" -> "is a ten-year-old boy"); plural ("years" -> "year").
new_why: Why: article ("is ten" -> "is a ten"); plural ("ten years old" -> "ten-year-old").

problem: wrong rule: raise/rise is word choice, not past tense
old_why: Why: past tense ("raised" -> "rose").
new_why: Why: word choice ("raised" -> "rose").

problem: wrong rule: besides/beside is word choice, not spelling
old_why: Why: spelling ("besides" -> "beside"); perfect tense ("is sitting all morning" -> "has been sitting").
new_why: Why: word choice ("besides" -> "beside"); perfect tense ("is sitting all morning" -> "has been sitting").

problem: trigger quote "we was" not in user sentence
old_why: Why: extra word ("reached to" -> "reached"); subject-verb agreement ("we was" -> "were").
new_why: Why: extra word ("reached to" -> "reached"); subject-verb agreement ("and was" -> "and were").

problem: word order change (moving "yesterday") not named
old_why: Why: past tense ("have sent yesterday" -> "sent").
new_why: Why: past tense ("have sent" -> "sent"); word order ("yesterday to my manager" -> "to my manager yesterday").

problem: perfect tense change ("they won" -> "they have won") not named
old_why: Why: word choice ("playing good" -> "playing well"); subject-verb agreement ("team are" -> "is"); punctuation (comma splice -> full stop).
new_why: Why: word choice ("good" -> "well"); subject-verb agreement ("are" -> "is"); punctuation ("," -> "."); perfect tense ("won" -> "have won").

problem: wrong rule: irregular past "losed" is past tense
old_why: Why: verb form ("losed" -> "lost"); word choice ("good" -> "well").
new_why: Why: past tense ("losed" -> "lost"); word choice ("good" -> "well").

problem: no-error line ungrammatical ("goes", "feels" is correct)
old_why: Why: no error (subject-verb agreement: "goes", "feels" is correct).
new_why: Why: no error (subject-verb agreement: "goes" and "feels" are correct).

problem: wrong rule: past habit "used to" is past tense, not continuous tense
old_why: Why: continuous tense ("is telling" -> "used to tell").
new_why: Why: past tense ("is telling" -> "used to tell").

problem: trigger wrong ("names" is not what changed)
old_why: Why: subject-verb agreement ("names" -> "What are the names").
new_why: Why: subject-verb agreement ("What is the names" -> "What are the names").

problem: no-error line ungrammatical (two phrases "is correct")
old_why: Why: no error (preposition: "interested in", "good at" is correct).
new_why: Why: no error (preposition: "interested in" and "good at" are correct).

problem: wrong rule: "for buying" -> "to buy" is verb form, not preposition
old_why: Why: preposition ("for buying" -> "to buy").
new_why: Why: verb form ("for buying" -> "to buy").

problem: punctuation trigger quoted corrected words, not the user's
old_why: Why: word choice ("got finished" -> "ran out"); punctuation ("battery ran out so" -> "out, so").
new_why: Why: word choice ("got finished" -> "ran out"); punctuation (missing comma -> comma before "so").

problem: no-error line ungrammatical ("lit", "looked" is correct)
old_why: Why: no error (past tense: "lit", "looked" is correct).
new_why: Why: no error (past tense: "lit" and "looked" are correct).

problem: wrong rule: "am waiting ... for half an hour" -> "have been waiting" is perfect tense
old_why: Why: continuous tense ("am waiting" -> "have been waiting").
new_why: Why: perfect tense ("am waiting" -> "have been waiting").

problem: trigger too broad ("right a good essay")
old_why: Why: spelling ("right a good essay" -> "write").
new_why: Why: spelling ("right" -> "write").
